title: Maps on cohomology of modules induced by f-maps (pullback, edge map)
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, $h_*$ the direct image, $(h_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(h^{-1}V)$ (an *$h$-map* from $\mathcal G$ to $\mathcal F$; equivalently, by the adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], a morphism $h^*\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$). For $p\ge0$ the map $\varphi^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ between the cohomology groups of [pqf-def-cohomology] is defined as follows. Choose injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $s_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $s_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with $\mathcal I^n=\mathcal J^n=0$ for $n<0$, so that $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$; choose a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules with $\mathcal J'^n=0$ for $n<0$ and a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] $\lambda:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $h_*$ applied termwise; and choose a morphism of complexes $\beta:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ with $\beta^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0\circ h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\circ\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J'^0$. Since $\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^n)=\mathcal I^n(h^{-1}Y)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^n)$, $\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$ is a morphism of complexes $\mu:\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$, and $\mu$ is a quasi-isomorphism (proof, Step 4). Then $\varphi^*=H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))$. Names: (a) the *pullback* $h^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,h^*\mathcal G)$ is $\varphi^*$ for the unit $\varphi=\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to h_*h^*\mathcal G$ of $h^*\dashv h_*$; (b) for an open $U\subseteq Y$, with $j:U\to Y$ the inclusion of the open subscheme and $\mathcal G|_U$ the restricted $\mathcal O_U$-module, $(\mathcal G|_U)(V)=\mathcal G(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ open [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], the *restriction* $\mathrm{res}^Y_U:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ is $\varphi^*$ for the $j$-map $\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to j_*(\mathcal G|_U)$ whose component on an open $V\subseteq Y$ is the restriction map $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V\cap U)$; (c) the *edge map* $e_{h,\mathcal F}:H^p(Y,h_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ is $\varphi^*$ for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$. (That $\varphi^*$ does not depend on the choices, is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear, is $\varphi_Y$ in degree $0$, is $H^p(\varphi)$ for $h=\mathrm{id}_Y$, and that $\mathrm{res}^Y_U$ is the pullback $j^*$ up to $j^*\mathcal G\cong\mathcal G|_U$, are statements about this definition, recorded in `pointers`.)

proof.text: Choose I = injectiveResolution F and J = injectiveResolution G using enoughInjectives for X.Modules and Y.Modules. For A = h_*I, extend A by zero along embeddingUpNat. Apply Mathlib CochainComplex.Plus.modelCategoryQuillen.exists_quasiIso_injective with lower bound zero. Its target L is strictly supported in nonnegative degrees. The canonical projection to truncGE along embeddingUpNat is therefore an isomorphism. Fullness of extendFunctor gives a natural-indexed map A -> L.truncGE' whose extension is the composite replacement. quasiIso_extendMap_iff reflects its quasi-isomorphism, and the component isomorphisms of restrictionToTruncGE' transfer injectivity. This is the proved private helper nat_complex_injective_resolution; no degreewise monomorphism is needed by ModuleCohomologyFMapData.

proof.text: Form gamma = phi >> h_*(I.augmentation in degree zero) >> lambda in degree zero. The chain-map equation for lambda and the augmentation equation for I show gamma is a cycle. Extend gamma along the monomorphic augmentation J.ι.f 0 using Injective.factorThru. The resulting degree-zero map composed with the differential kills the augmentation. J.exact₀.descToInjective supplies the degree-one map. Inductively J.exact_succ.descToInjective supplies each next map; the preceding chain equation and d squared equal zero verify its compatibility. CochainComplex.mkHom packages the maps as beta. Its degree-zero component gives exactly the required augmentation equation. This is lift_to_nat_injectives, a specialization of the augmentation-lifting argument, proved directly rather than using the general lift or homotopy uniqueness theorem.

proof.text: For every term I^n use the presheaf.mapIso of the equality h inverse-image of the whole Y equals the whole X. These component isomorphisms commute with the differentials by naturality of the underlying presheaf morphism. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents makes the canonical complex isomorphism a, with its inverse components definitionally the specified restriction maps. This is pushforward_sections_iso.

proof.text: Extend I and K by zero to integer indices. Compose mapExtendIso for h_* with extendMap lambda to obtain an integer-indexed quasi-isomorphism h_*(extend I) -> extend K. Apply quasiIso_globalSections_pushforward_injectives: all terms of the extended complexes are injective, and negative terms are zero. Application of sections to mapExtendIso is an isomorphism, so remove it from the composite. The natural isomorphism embeddingUpNat.mapExtendFunctorNatIso for the additive abelian-group-valued global-sections functor identifies the remaining map with extension of the natural-indexed sections map. Transfer quasi-isomorphism by Arrow.isoMk and quasiIso_of_arrow_mk_iso, then reflect by quasiIso_extendMap_iff. Thus Γ(Y,lambda) induces invertible homology maps. The isomorphism a also induces invertible homology maps, and Functor.map_comp proves invertibility of the composite. This is nat_quasiIso_globalSections_pushforward_injectives followed by the final record construction.
